In [[probability theory]], the '''ladder height process''' is a record of the largest or smallest value a given [[stochastic process]] has achieved up to the specified point in time.<ref>{{Cite book | first1 = S. R. | last1 = Asmussen| doi = 10.1007/0-387-21525-5_8 | chapter = Random Walks | title = Applied Probability and Queues | series = Stochastic Modelling and Applied Probability | volume = 51 | pages = 220–243 | year = 2003 | isbn = 978-0-387-00211-8 | pmid =  | pmc = }}</ref>

The [[Wiener-Hopf factorization]] gives the transition probability kernel in the discrete time case.<ref>{{Cite book | last1 = Miyazawa | first1 = M. | chapter = A paradigm of Markov additive processes for queues and their networks| doi = 10.1142/9789812777164_0015 | title = Matrix-Analytic Methods - Theory and Applications - Proceedings of the Fourth International Conference | pages = 265–289 | year = 2002 | isbn = 9789812380517 | pmid =  | pmc = }}</ref>
